text_nodes.text: It judges flood risk on the device
UT San Antonio's prototype runs its AI on the device, with no server. Its release says risk at San Antonio's low-water crossings often climbs before regional alerts sound. Drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: Radar can read the storm low

UT San Antonio's release says regional models can miss very local flash floods. UT Arlington checked radar against more than 300 rain gauges and found it can read storm totals roughly 20% low under some conditions.

text_nodes.text: TinyML shrinks a machine learning model to run on a small, low-power microcontroller. The model on the node judges imminent flood risk from current and recent readings without a central server.
Over a half-mile in town, up to five miles open
The node's LoRa radio reaches more than a half-mile through city streets and up to five miles in open areas, the release says. No site is named, so the circles show scale only.
